authoringStatement: X1 expectations were authored before production transport behavior existed. Mechanical values come from declared exact-time formulas and the frozen X0/P0/A0 contracts; timing feel and timbre judgments remain explicit human release work.

classificationPolicy.primary-standard: A current normative or editor-draft Web platform standard.
classificationPolicy.reviewed-contract: A normative repository architecture or package decision.
classificationPolicy.legacy-observation: A reproduced legacy failure the replacement must not preserve.
classificationPolicy.mechanical-derivation: A direct result of a declared formula, integer algorithm, or cap.
classificationPolicy.human-review: A judgment that automation cannot honestly certify.

authorities.source: Web Audio API 1.1 Editor's Draft, https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/
supports: AudioContext currentTime as the only musical clock
twelve-node/thirteen-edge persistent topology superseding the informal separate click bus
exact rational beats with PPQ 960 tick mirrors
24-tick release gap and one-tick gate floor
interrupted projects to paused with the stable transport.interrupted code because the frozen A0 status union has no interrupted member and failed would misreport a recoverable state
0.2 s lookahead ceiling leaves an explicit 0.05 s margin under the X0 admission window so lateness refusals are unreachable
queue bound of 32 commands refuses pathological bursts while holding every human-scale interaction
count-in is exactly one bar; clicks use the vibraphone recipe, accent MIDI 88 velocity 112, beat MIDI 81 velocity 84, 0.06 s gate, reserved x1:click: identifiers
the audio-envelope floor max(gateSeconds, 0.005) applies only to Web Audio release times and never to beats, ticks, or MIDI export
stop in ready is a vacuous receipt so global Stop is always safe after initialization
loop bindings keep the plan revision because loop is ephemeral transport state; tempo bindings require a strictly newer revision because tempo is document data

authorities.source: docs/X1_TRANSPORT_CONTRACT.md section 4, set-performance amendment (jcpe-7ftl), mirroring the accepted set-tempo epoch law
